method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

supports: x-management-052: identify/avoid conflicts, disclose and ethically manage without personal gain overriding duty
sourceChecks.scope: Targeted ethical principle support; jurisdiction and exact arrangement still need specification for legal conclusions.

supports: x-management-060: prompt employer/team discussion and continued access/continuity despite conscientious objection

items.assessment: Formal financial supports address need while avoiding personal debt in the current therapeutic relationship.
Transparent conflict management is directionally correct, but the explanation could imply disclosure alone legitimizes a paid referral arrangement.
issues: Transparent conflict management is directionally correct, but the explanation could imply disclosure alone legitimizes a paid referral arrangement.
proposedChanges: Make key explicit: Prioritize client needs and disclose and resolve the commission conflict before recommending. Explain that disclosure alone does not make personal financial benefit acceptable; use organizational/regulator safeguards and impartial options. Attach jurisdiction-relevant conflict guidance.

items.assessment: Respectful discussion and gift-boundary policy handle costly gift without treating client initiation or final visit as automatic permission.
Private trip with a current client changes relationship regardless of coverage or duration; boundary discussion is defensible.
Available qualified alternate permits disclosure/reassignment for close friendship; concealed exchange bypasses appropriate coordination.
Regulatory approval/testimonials do not justify omitting limitations; balanced independent evidence is appropriate.
Client-focus key is sound; written client permission before self-disclosure is an implausible invented requirement.
issues: Client-focus key is sound; written client permission before self-disclosure is an implausible invented requirement.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: The topic was unrelated to wound-care teaching. Explain that topic alone is not decisive because limited therapeutic self-disclosure may be appropriate; prolonged displacement of client needs is the concern.

items.assessment: Pre-shift dizziness/slowing needs early fitness disclosure and coverage; routine work also requires unimpaired judgment.
Observable slurring/dropped medication warrants immediate client protection and supervisory escalation without inferring the cause.
Early conscientious concern, continuity and respectful role-appropriate information align with duty-to-care guidance; withdrawal before cover creates gap.
Individual pain assessment plus addressing discriminatory behaviour responds to both current care and harmful conduct.
Stated name and reliable identification can coexist; unilateral record replacement and family override are inappropriate.
Stable routine care can accommodate prayer while preserving time-sensitive needs and individual preferences.
Accessible durable information with usability check supports home independence better than one reading or unchanged family copy.
Capable client permission defines supporter participation without transferring treatment authority.
Collaborative goal review is sound; suspending all therapy until client accepts team goal is a conspicuously coercive distractor.
issues: Collaborative goal review is sound; suspending all therapy until client accepts team goal is a conspicuously coercive distractor.
proposedChanges: Replace option3 with: Keep the original stair goal and provide only a leaflet on wheelchair access. Explain that information alone does not integrate the client participation priority into measurable rehabilitation goals.

items.assessment: Predictability/permission address distress from unannounced approach; repeated exposure or restricting all care does not create a collaborative plan.
Urgency and safe alternatives are defensible temporary allocation criteria; convenience and fixed schedules alone overlook need.
Evidence/local authorization key is sound; trial on every client is unrealistic broad adoption.
issues: Evidence/local authorization key is sound; trial on every client is unrealistic broad adoption.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Trial the free sample on the next similar wound before checking evidence or authorization. Explain that a small trial still needs suitability and approved process.

items.assessment: Workflow review, authorized learning and practical safeguards address near-miss recurrence beyond an individual reminder.
Client explanation directly measures intended learning; leaflets, staff attendance and time are credible process proxies.
Checklist evaluation is sound; liking its appearance is weak filler as an adoption criterion.
issues: Checklist evaluation is sound; liking its appearance is weak filler as an adoption criterion.
proposedChanges: Replace option2 with: Expand it because handover took less time in the trial. Explain that efficiency alone does not establish completeness, usability or unintended harms.

items.assessment: Client assessment/care/response belong in clinical chart; reporting/discipline do not substitute for care facts.
Known facts through coordinated disclosure are appropriate without legal speculation, guarantees or waiting for complete investigation.
Approved audit still requires data minimization and secure purpose-limited handling; future convenience is not authorization.
Escalating discrepancy with safe interim practice avoids both uncritical routine and uncoordinated blanket stopping.
Long unused skill needs current learning and supported demonstration; old certification/observation alone do not verify present competence.
Focused question, findings and follow-up support consultation; consultation does not transfer every nursing responsibility.
Direct repeat/confirmation supports closed-loop understanding of authorized verbal instruction before action.
Known allergy handover omission after interruption needs deliberate checkpoint recovery before treatment begins.
New crushing pressure outranks routine signature; qualified assessment and escalation are appropriate. Foundation priority level would be more accurate.
Explicit dose coverage or adjusted attendance protects time-critical care without arbitrary early/late administration.
New instability requires assessment/stabilization and coordinated transport support regardless of scarce test slot.
Possible blocked artificial airway requires immediate response; comparison against a blanket request is foundation-level prioritization.
Delayed departure does not end current care needs; reassessed interim meals/medication plan prevents transition gaps.
Worsening condition despite unanswered urgent referral requires an available escalation pathway matching present urgency.
Time-sensitive tasks, reassessment flexibility and coordination support adaptive shift planning.
Nearby qualified response while assigned nurse handles another emergency supports immediate safety and team coordination.
Proactive wishes/order clarification is sound; greatest signature count is a weak invented validity test.
issues: Proactive wishes/order clarification is sound; greatest signature count is a weak invented validity test.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Use the form with the latest visible date without checking whether it reflects current wishes and valid orders. Explain that apparent recency alone does not resolve applicability and validity.

items.assessment: Core distinction is correct, but withholding analgesia until no-CPR rescinded is an implausibly extreme distractor.
issues: Core distinction is correct, but withholding analgesia until no-CPR rescinded is an implausibly extreme distractor.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Use only nonpharmacologic comfort measures despite an available prescribed analgesic. Explain that a no-CPR plan does not itself exclude prescribed symptom treatment; decisions follow broader goals and assessment. Classify foundation.

items.assessment: Exploring capable clients own information preferences respects autonomy without assuming family secrecy request controls disclosure.
Ethics consultation can support unresolved values/consent conflict without replacing clinical/legal process or assigning unilateral authority.
Comfort plus desired alertness match expressed goal better than pain alone, dose quantity or task counts.
Local advance-planning resources avoid asserting a universal directive rule and support discussion before crisis.
Facilitating client-directed Elder access avoids substituting generic or staff-selected cultural assumptions.
Interpreter must relay client response; role clarification preserves language access and decision ownership.
Accessible communication/direct engagement/support-based understanding respects disability without presuming incapacity.
Concern, information and follow-up provide continuity after capable refusal without judgmental labels.
Private evidence/standards review and agreed plan prevent inconsistent care while meaningful client participation can follow.
Completing required verification preserves personal accountability despite senior pressure or common shortcut culture.
